# Visonaut capture in Ariakit

The existing `@visual` tests remain the capture source. Their `visual()` helper sends captures to Visonaut when the trusted executor is installed. Each visual test declares an explicit item ID through `setVisonautItem(...)`; a test title or file rename does not change it. Existing capture IDs distinguish separate prepared states. Generic previews use their authored route IDs and framework. The trusted `items.json` freezes the item and variant keys required in each browser. The runner requires every collected `@visual` test to capture and every registered pair to appear. New explicit pairs may appear as additions; after their first complete main capture, add them to `items.json` so later runs require them. To remove a pair, first remove its requirement from the trusted registry on main while the old test still captures it, then remove the capture in a separate change. The registry change is the deliberate authorization for that removal. During diagnostic runs, Ariakit's current screenshot job stays required. The old screenshot update workflow is removed only after the Visonaut check is ready to replace it.

The pinned reusable workflow takes one fixed browser project per job and requires the whole `@visual` collection. The `@visonaut/playwright` reporter accepts only final successful Playwright attempts and writes a complete manifest. The render job uploads only an encrypted shard. A separate submission job checks out only the pinned trusted executor, obtains the transfer key from Visonaut after signed-job verification, decrypts the shard, and submits it to private quarantine. The key is not an Ariakit Actions secret. The service independently verifies the workflow SHA, trusted-main plan, tested commit, successful job, and receipt artifact.

Before the first npm release, `bootstrap.mjs` requests a job-bound GitHub OIDC token and downloads only the two audited future-public client tarballs from the Visonaut preview service. The service accepts only the signed render or capture job in the pinned reusable workflow, checks the live run and tested commit, then reads two exact private object keys named by trusted-main SHA-256 pins. The script checks both the pinned digest and byte count before unpacking into the executor. Package bytes are present in the render job, but no R2 token, signed URL, service source, or private review data enters it. GitHub's `id-token: write` permission applies to the whole render job, including candidate test steps. Removing OIDC variables from those shell commands reduces accidental exposure but is not a security boundary. The Visonaut upload API separately rejects render-job tokens.

After all launch gates pass and both packages are public, remove `bootstrap.mjs` and the temporary service endpoint, then pin both releases in `package-lock.json` by npm integrity. Regenerate `.github/visonaut-plan.json` and the two workflow/source commit pins. Run the complete hosted cycle again before required-check cutover.

Keep the workflow and source pins on reviewed `main` commits. The 288 environment profile digests live only in the trusted plan. New runner images or fonts require a new hosted probe and a reviewed plan update. Do not pass the transfer private key to the render job or upload plaintext images, manifests, or client packages as public GitHub artifacts.
